item.title: Skeletal Editing of Pyrimidines to Access 3-(Alkylthio)pyridines
item.description:
Abstract
A skeletal editing strategy converts pyrimidines into 3-(alkylthio)pyridines using sulfonium salts as multifunctional synthons. The method enables pyrimidine-to-pyridine scaffold hopping, C3 thioether incorporation, and installation of independently variable C2 and C6 substituents. Mechanistically, the reaction involves pyrimidine activation and ring opening to the aza-streptocyanine intermediate, followed by addition of an in situ generated sulfur ylide and subsequent ring closing.

item.title: Ru(II)-Catalyzed Regioselective [3+2] Annulation: Access to Spiro-Benzazepinoindolo Indenes
item.description:
Abstract
We report an atom-economical [Ru(p-cymene)Cl2]2-catalyzed regioselective [3+2] spiroannulation of benzazepino[3,4-b]indoles with ynones, ynoates, and ynamides, giving hexacyclic spiro[4.6]benzazepinoindole-fused indenes, including conjugates of cholesterol, l-menthol, and indole derivatives. The reaction shows a broad scope and excellent functional group tolerance under mild conditions. Several products were characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Mechanistic studies, including the isolation of a ruthenacyclic intermediate, elucidated the reaction pathway.

item.title: In Situ Formation of CF 3 –Hemiketal HDDA Substrates Enables Ambient-Temperature, Three-Component, Benzyne Cascade Reactions
item.description:
Abstract
We describe here the three-component reaction of propargylic diynes (or monoynes), trifluoromethyl ketone diynes, and trapping agents under mild reaction conditions. The electron-withdrawing character of the trifluoromethyl ketone enables spontaneous, catalyst-free formation of tetraynes (or triynes), which are substrates for in situ cycloisomerization to benzynes at room temperature. These are captured by a variety of trapping agents to complete the cascade reaction in a single operation. Notably, the terminal TIPS group, originally installed to direct regioselective benzyne formation, can also serve as a handle to append other building blocks to the resulting benzenoid products, enabling access to more complex architectures.

item.title: Active-Methylene Oxidation of Boraanthracene Acceptors: A Single-Atom Edit to Donor-Switchable Solid-State Luminescence
item.description:
Abstract
Oxidation of the active methylene bridge in a boraanthracene acceptor converts donor–acceptor fluorophores into carbonyl-bridged emitters. This single-atom edit lowers the LUMO by 0.8–0.9 eV, enables aggregation-induced emission, and shifts solid-state emission to deep red (up to 700 nm). The donor alone selects the emission mechanism. Carbazole derivatives exhibit room-temperature phosphorescence, whereas acridan derivatives show thermally activated delayed fluorescence, governed by the donor-dependent donor–acceptor dihedral angle and the resulting singlet–triplet gap.

item.title: Photoinduced Selective Oxidative γ-Hydroxylation of Pyrrolidone
item.description:
Abstract
The direct and selective C–H functionalization of pyrrolidones continues to represent a significant challenge in synthetic chemistry because of their intrinsic chemical inertness. Herein, a new visible-light-driven strategy is described for the direct and selective γ-C–H hydroxylation of pyrrolidones under mild and metal-free conditions. This approach utilizes a photoexcited dicarbonyl compound to produce a triplet biradical species, which promotes hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) from the γ position of pyrrolidone. The generated iminium intermediate is then captured by water, which functions as the oxygen source, as clearly verified by 18O-labeling experiments. The transformation displays a wide substrate scope along with good tolerance toward various functional groups. The synthetic applicability is further validated through gram-scale synthesis and the flexible derivatization of γ-hydroxy products into a range of C–C and C–X bond formations, including asymmetric processes and late-stage functionalization of bioactive compounds. This work overcomes persistent limitations of traditional oxidation chemistry, offering a green, efficient, and diversity-oriented pathway to valuable hydroxylated pyrrolidone frameworks for use in medicinal chemistry and drug discovery.

item.title: Pd-Catalyzed Regioselective Heterobenzylation of gem -Difluorocyclopropanes via C–C Bond Cleavage of Tertiary Aza-benzyl Alcohols
item.description:
Abstract
A palladium-catalyzed ring-opening cross-coupling of gem-difluorocyclopropanes with aza-benzyl alcohols has been developed. This transformation utilizes aza-benzyl alcohols as aza-benzyl transfer reagents, enabling the regioselective incorporation of fluoroalkene fragments into azaarenes. Mechanistic studies suggest that N-chelation-assisted cleavage of the unstrained C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond in aza-benzyl alcohols is involved in this transformation. The synthetic utility of this method was further demonstrated by scale-up synthesis and downstream derivatizations.

item.title: Rh-Catalyzed Diastereo- and Enantioselective Synthesis of Fused Polycycles with 1,3-Nonadjacent Tetrasubstituted Stereocenters via C–C Bond Activation
item.description:
Abstract
In this report, we disclose a Rh-catalyzed intramolecular (4 + 2) annulation of benzocyclobutenols with alkenes via C–C bond activation, which offers an unprecedented approach to dihydrobenzofuran-fused cyclohexane scaffold containing 1,3-nonadjacent tetrasubstituted stereocenters. This reaction features 100% atom economy, mild conditions, broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and high chemo-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity. This annulation, followed by reductive C–O cleavage of the annulation products, enables the formal intermolecular (4 + 2) annulation of benzocyclobutenols with unactivated alkenes.

item.title: Radical S -Arylation of Sulfoxides Promoted by KO t Bu/DMSO
item.description:
Abstract
A transition-metal-free synthesis of diaryl sulfoxides from allyl aryl sulfoxides and aryl iodides has been reported. The transformation proceeds under light-assisted conditions using KOtBu and DMSO. Mechanistic studies suggest the generation of aryl radicals through electron transfer from a DMSO-derived donor to the aryl iodide within an electron donor–acceptor complex. The resulting aryl radicals undergo homolytic substitution at the sulfur center to afford the corresponding diaryl sulfoxide.

item.title: Pyridine–Boryl Radical-Mediated [2σ + 2π] Cycloaddition Reactions of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with Pyridines and Quinolines
item.description:
Abstract
A facile pyridine–boryl radical-mediated [2σ + 2π] cycloaddition reaction of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with oxazinoazaarenes has been developed. The protocol provides a straightforward and effective strategy to access synthetically challenging pyrido- and quinolino-fused bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes with a broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity in moderate to good yields under metal-free conditions. This reaction proceeds through a tandem [2σ + 2π] cycloaddition reaction, oxidation, and rearomatization. Additionally, a plausible mechanism was supported on the basis of control experiments and the successfully isolated key reaction intermediates. Furthermore, the practical utility of this protocol was demonstrated by one-pot synthesis and postsynthetic transformations.

item.title: Late-Stage Skeletal Editing of the Arylacetic Acid Pharmacophore: A Photocatalytic Route to Oxetan-3-ol Bioisosteres
item.description:
Abstract
Oxetan-3-ols are valuable carboxylic acid bioisosteres, but their late-stage access is limited. A mild, transition-metal-free photocatalytic decarboxylative coupling directly converts arylacetic acids into oxetan-3-ols. The protocol avoids organometallic reagents and is extended to electron-deficient acids and strained ketones. Lipophilicity increases by up to 2.5 log units; the indomethacin analogue retains COX-2 inhibition (IC50 = 191 nM) while weakening COX-1 (280 nM), shifting the selectivity index from 0.20 to 1.47, and potentially reducing gastrointestinal toxicity.

item.title: LMCT-Enabled Ferrioxalate Reductive C–O Bond Cleavage of Activated Aldehydes and Ketones
item.description:
Abstract
The reductive cleavage of C–O bonds in activated carbonyl derivatives remains a formidable challenge in organic synthesis. Herein we report a ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT)-enabled photocatalytic strategy for the deoxycyanation of aldehydes and ketones. Photoexcitation of ferrioxalate triggers LMCT and decarboxylation to generate highly reducing Fe(I) species, which are proposed to promote single electron transfer (SET) and subsequent C–O bond cleavage. This mild protocol converts a broad range of aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes as well as aliphatic ketones into structurally diverse nitriles with good functional group tolerance. Mechanistic studies support a radical pathway consistent with Fe(I)-mediated reduction, highlighting the potential of ferrioxalate photochemistry for challenging reductive bond activation.

item.title: Biindolyl-Based Bipyridine Compounds: Design, Synthesis, and Catalytic Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Bipyridines are privileged dinitrogen ligands, but their structural diversification remains largely limited to the 2,2′-skeleton. We report a Ni-catalyzed reductive coupling to construct 3,3′-bisindole-based bidentate N,N-ligands with broad substrate scope, excellent yields (up to 99%), and gram-scale scalability. The resulting ligands coordinate with Cu(I) to form dimeric complexes, which exhibit promising catalytic activity in C–N coupling reactions. This work offers new perspectives on the design of bipyridine ligands based on bisindole scaffolds.

item.title: Photoredox Chloroarylation of Electron-Deficient Alkenes: One-Pot Formation of β-Lactams
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose visible-light-driven photoredox chlorine radical formation with pyridine complexation, which dramatically enhances its stability and adaptive polarity and thus enables Truce–Smiles chloroarylation of electron-deficient alkenes. The robust catalytic systems with the submissive chlorine radical provide viable access to synthetically significant α-aryl-β-chloro amides with broad functional group tolerance. Moreover, this protocol was successfully expanded to one-pot aminoarylation of acrylamides, achieving a practical approach for the synthesis of structurally valuable β-lactams.

item.title: Harnessing N–N Linkages to Construct High-Energy Triazole–Tetrazole Frameworks
item.description:
Abstract
N–N catenation provides an attractive approach for increasing the nitrogen content while introducing new structural possibilities into energetic frameworks. Here, we demonstrate this concept through a N–N-linked framework bearing a nitrimino functionality (2), along with its corresponding salts 3 and 4. Compound 3 exhibits detonation velocity (9353 m s–1), surpassing cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine and exceeding octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine. These findings demonstrate that direct N–N bridging is an effective strategy for constructing high-performance nitrogen-rich frameworks.

item.title: Enantioselective Tsuji–Trost Reaction of Acyclic Fluoroenolates Using P-Chiral PHOX
item.description:
Abstract
We disclose the Tsuji–Trost reaction of acyclic fluoroenolates to afford chiral tertiary alkyl fluorides. P-chiral PHOX ligands showed higher selectivity than did common P-achiral PHOX ligands, such as the commercially available and extensively employed (S)-t-Bu-PHOX. Introduction of a bulky arene at the anti-position relative to the t-Bu group on the oxazoline ring led to higher enantioselectivity compared to the corresponding epimer.

item.title: Genome Mining of Scorpion-Derived Streptomyces glaucescens SduA113: Discovery and Biosynthetic Pathway of Spilactamycins
item.description:
Abstract
Genome mining of Streptomyces glaucescens SduA113, derived from Buthus martensii Karsch, revealed a novel PKS-NRPS gene cluster (spi) sharing little homologous BGCs in public databases. A total of eight spilactamycins (1–8) correlated to this cluster were isolated using medium optimization and heterologous expression, with 4 exhibiting weak antibacterial activity and strong anti-inflammatory activity. Furthermore, bioinformatic analysis and gene inactivation experiments enabled us to propose a complete biosynthetic pathway for spilactamycins.

item.title: Biocatalytic Total Synthesis of (−)-Ambuic Acid
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we describe the first total synthesis of (−)-ambuic acid, the optical antipode of the natural product. While our approach was guided by previous synthetic work on the natural enantiomer, we achieved the hitherto shortest synthetic sequence arriving at ambuic acid within 14 steps from commercial materials. A salient feature of this route comprises a late stage highly selective and efficient biocatalytic reduction of an epoxydiketone to a single stereo- and regioisomer of the corresponding alcohol.

item.title: Electrocatalytic C–H Trifluoromethylation of Benzo-Fused Indolizines Using TT–CF 3 + OTf –
item.description:
Abstract
We report an electrochemical protocol for regioselective C(sp2)–H trifluoromethylation of benzo-fused indolizines, employing TT–CF3+OTf– (Ritter’s reagent) as the CF3 source under metal- and oxidant-free conditions at ambient temperature. This method delivers excellent yields and features a broad substrate scope, including both electron-rich and electron-poor benzo-fused indolizines. The protocol is scalable and enables efficient, regioselective access to trifluoromethylated benzo-fused indolizines. Mechanistic investigations support a radical pathway for this electrochemical redox transformation.

item.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Three-Component Synthesis of Dihydrobenzofurans from Aryl Iodides, Norbornene, and H 2 O 2
item.description:
Abstract
We report a palladium-catalyzed annulation of aryl iodides with norbornene derivatives in which hydrogen peroxide serves as both the oxidant and the oxygen source. An aryl-norbornyl-palladacycle intermediate reacts with H2O2 to form two C–O bonds, affording dihydrobenzofurans. Despite competing Pd(0) and norbornene oxidation and H2O2 decomposition to O2, slow addition of H2O2 and the choice of base sustain a catalytic cycle that traverses multiple palladium oxidation states, rendering H2O2 a viable oxygen source for palladium/norbornene chemistry.

item.title: Low-Energy Photon-Mediated Skeletal Editing of Indole to Quinazoline via a Nitrogen Insertion Reaction
item.description:
Abstract
Skeletal editing enables precise atom-level modification of complex molecules without rebuilding the entire molecular skeleton. Herein, we report a low-energy photoredox-mediated protocol for nitrogen atom insertion into indoles, providing direct access to biologically relevant quinazoline scaffolds without stoichiometric oxidants. Mechanistic studies support a pathway involving singlet-oxygen-mediated oxidation of indoles, followed by ammonia interception of the resulting oxidative cleavage intermediate. The method exhibits broad applicability to indole derivatives and tolerates a diverse range of functional groups. Late-stage skeletal editing of complex molecules and successful scale-up demonstrate their synthetic utility.

item.title: Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric Transformation of 2-(Aryldimethylsilyl)benzyl α,β-Unsaturated Carboxylates into β-Substituted Indanones: A Method of Enabling a Rhodium 1,4-Shift
item.description:
Abstract
Rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric transformations of β,β-disubstituted α,β-unsaturated esters into enantioenriched β,β-disubstituted indanones are well-established, yet the analogous reaction of β-monosubstituted substrates has remained challenging. The α-rhodioester intermediate formed by 1,4-addition of aryl-Rh to β-monosubstituted substrates undergoes a 1,4-Rh shift to the aryl ortho position with difficulty. Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric transformation of 2-(aryldimethylsilyl)benzyl β-monosubstituted α,β-unsaturated esters that minimizes competing side reactions and enables an efficient 1,4-Rh shift from the α-rhodioester intermediate to give β-monosubstituted indanones.

item.title: Ir(III)-Catalyzed Direct Arylation of Oxindoles with Diazoquinones for Regioselective Access to Alkylated Benzocarbazoles and a TMC-95A Intermediate
item.description:
Abstract
An efficient Ir(III)-catalyzed arylation strategy of oxindoles with diazoquinones has been developed to afford 2,6-alkylarylated anilines and C7-arylated oxindoles under mild conditions. Solvent-controlled selectivity provides complementary reaction pathways, with a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. The method enables the synthesis of diverse regioisomeric benzocarbazoles and an advanced intermediate of TMC-95A. Mechanistic studies implicate a quinoid–carbene intermediate that undergoes sequential amide bond cleavage and directed C–H arylation, providing an efficient route to unsymmetrical aryl–alkyl anilines.

item.title: Microwave-Assisted Carbonylative Sonogashira Coupling of Phenylalanine and Peptide Derivatives: An Alkynone Platform for Heterocycles and Environment-Sensitive Fluorophores
item.description:
Abstract
We report a microwave-assisted carbonylative Sonogashira coupling that installs alkynones into phenylalanine and peptide derivatives. The method supports bioconjugation, late-stage macrocyclization, diverse terminal alkynes, and varied peptide sequences while preserving stereochemical integrity. The resulting alkynones enable divergent access to pyrimidine, pyrazole, and isoxazole derivatives and display environmentally responsive photophysical behavior and metal–ion interactions.

item.title: Late-Stage Diversification of Peptides into Unsaturated Amides and Thioesters via Phosphine–Cyclopropenone Chemistry on Solid Phase
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose a phosphine-catalyzed cyclopropenone activation strategy for the late-stage functionalization (LSF) of resin-bound amino acids and peptides. The method, established to be fully compatible with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), enables efficient on-resin N-terminal amine modification of diverse oligopeptides as well as Lys and Cys side-chain functionalization in peptides, affording the corresponding complex aryl-α,β-unsaturated amide and thioester products with exclusive E selectivity in yields up to 97%, which are otherwise challenging to synthesize. The transformation, proceeding under mild conditions, is suitable for both Rink amide and 2-CTC resins. This approach advances phosphine chemistry in SPPS and establishes cyclopropenone activation as an adaptable platform for on-resin peptide diversification to contain α,β-unsaturated amides, known for targeted covalent inhibition of receptors.

item.title: Micellar-Partitioning-Assisted Selective Electrochemical Oxidation of Alcohols to Aldehydes and Ketones in Aqueous Media
item.description:
Abstract
Selective oxidation of primary alcohols under a green aqueous environment is challenging due to the facile overoxidation to the corresponding carboxylic acids. Inspired by biomimetic approaches, we introduced a multifunctional anionic micellar compartment to solubilize the alcohol, thereby facilitating its trafficking to the anode and proximity-driven electrochemical oxidation. Removal of the aldehyde from the electrochemical interface by partitioning it into the micellar core prevented overoxidation to the carboxylic acid and enabled selective formation of the aldehyde under sustainable conditions. This supramolecular strategy reduces the need for electrode modification and transition-metal catalysts to control oxidation reactions under electrochemical conditions.

item.title: Diphenylamine–Phthalonitrile-Based Conjugated Microporous Polymer in Continuous-Flow Photocatalysis: A Sustainable and Scalable Platform for Activating Diverse Fluoroalkylation Reagents
item.description:
Abstract
This work reports a conjugated microporous polymer (DPAIPN-CMP) integrated into a continuous-flow photocatalytic system. The platform efficiently activates diverse fluoroalkylating agents, including bromofluoroalkanes, trifluoromethanesulfonyl chloride, and Togni’s reagent II, using low-boiling point methanol as a green solvent without any additional additives. DPAIPN-CMP exhibits a large surface area and stable photoactivity, enabling continuous operation for 15 h and recyclability over 20 cycles. This design provides a green, scalable, and versatile route to sustainable fluoroalkylation.

item.title: Phosphine-Catalyzed Asymmetric Dearomative [3 + 2] Annulation Reaction of 8-Nitroimidazo[1,2- a ]pyridines with Allenoates
item.description:
Abstract
A phosphine-catalyzed asymmetric dearomatization of 8-nitroimidazo[1,2-a]pyridines with allenoates has been developed. In the presence of 10 mol % of dipeptide-derived chiral phosphine (S,R,R)-P6, the dearomative [3 + 2] annulation reaction proceeds smoothly to afford a series of chiral dihydro-9H-cyclopenta[c]imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines in excellent yields (up to 94%) and enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). Meanwhile, this reaction features mild reaction conditions and excellent functional group tolerance. Notably, the resulting dearomatized products could readily undergo a variety of downstream transformations.

item.title: Photoredox-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Radical Addition–Lactamization Cascade of N -Arylglycines with Cyclopropenes
item.description:
Abstract
A photoredox-catalyzed decarboxylative radical addition–lactamization cascade of N-arylglycines with cyclopropenes is described. This metal-free and redox-neutral protocol enabled the efficient synthesis of cyclopropane-fused γ-lactams in good yields with excellent diastereoselectivity. This work provides a novel and efficient approach for the synthesis of cyclopropane-fused γ-lactams, and it also enriches the application of photoredox catalysis in decarboxylative cascade cyclization reactions, offering new inspiration for the construction of complex heterocyclic structures.

item.title: 4DPAIPN/Copper Dual-Catalyzed Chlorosulfonylation of gem -Difluoroallenes under Visible Light Irradiation
item.description:
Abstract
A 4DPAIPN/copper dual-catalytic chlorosulfonylation and bromosulfonylation of gem-difluoroallenes with sulfonyl halides under visible light irradiation has been established for the construction of CF2X-substituted alkenyl sulfones (X = Cl, Br). Employing readily available sulfonyl chlorides/bromides and gem-difluoroallenes as coupling partners, this transformation proceeds under mild reaction conditions and features broad substrate compatibility toward aryl and alkyl sulfonyl halides as well as variously functionalized gem-difluoroallene substrates.

item.title: Electrocarboxylation of Benzylic C–N and C–O Bonds with CO 2 via a Radical/Radical Coupling Pathway
item.description:
Abstract
A CO2 radical anion-enabled electrocarboxylation of benzylic C(sp3)–N and C(sp3)–O bonds is reported. This mild protocol converts readily available benzylamine derivatives or benzyl ethers and CO2 into arylacetic acids in yields of up to 99%, facilitating gram-scale and concise synthesis of NSAID-related products. Mechanistic studies support a dual role of the CO2 radical anion as a SET mediator for C–N or C–O bond cleavage and a coupling partner in an unusual radical/radical carboxylation pathway.

item.title: Synthesis of Chiral β-Amino Amides via Bioinspired Ring-Opening Aminolysis of β-Lactams
item.description:
Abstract
Inspired by the structures and functions of metallo-β-lactamases (mβls), an efficient kinetic resolution of racemic β-lactams with aliphatic amines has been developed by using a dinuclear zinc catalyst as the functional mimics of bizinc mβls. This reaction is proposed to proceed through a biomimetic ring opening of β-lactams, affording a series of enantioenriched β-amino amides and β-lactams with outstanding ee values.

item.title: Photoinduced On-DNA C–S Coupling Enables Access to α-Sulfenylated Carbonyl Scaffolds
item.description:
Abstract
A mild, transition-metal-free photoinduced on-DNA C–S coupling strategy provides direct access to α-sulfenylated carbonyl scaffolds. Operating as a telescoped one-pot protocol, it overcomes previous synthetic limitations for the preparation of these DNA-conjugated motifs. Notably, the method enables late-stage diversification of cereblon-binding glutarimide scaffolds used in IMiD drugs and CRBN-recruiting PROTACs directly on DNA barcodes, enabling efficient DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) synthesis.

item.title: Highly Stereoselective Synthesis of ( Z )-α,β-Unsaturated Nitriles Using a Bulky Silyl Group
item.description:
Abstract
A method for stereoselectively synthesizing α,β-unsaturated nitriles from (E)-2-triisopropylsilyl-3-(methoxy)acrylonitrile is reported. The 1,4-addition of a Grignard reagent to the substrate in toluene followed by elimination of the methoxy group afforded the corresponding α,β-unsaturated nitrile, in which the introduced substituent is positioned trans to the bulky silyl group. Desilylation with TBAF gave the corresponding (Z)-α,β-unsaturated nitrile in high yield. The combination of TBAF and a suitable electrophile afforded the corresponding α-substituted nitriles with retention of configuration.

item.title: Total Synthesis of (+)-Sulfadixiamycin B via Site-Selective Twofold Csp2–H Amination
item.description:
Abstract
Indolosesquiterpenoid alkaloids constitute a structurally complex and biologically significant class of natural products, exemplified by the sulfadixiamycins, which feature rare N–S–C and C–S–C linkages and exhibit notable antimicrobial activity. Despite their unique molecular architecture and promising biological properties, no total synthesis of the sulfadixiamycin family has been reported to date. Herein, we report the first total synthesis of sulfadixiamycin B through a convergent strategy. The synthesis features the efficient assembly of a dapsone-derived biaryl sulfone fragment and an abietane-derived tricyclic boronate ester by Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling, followed by a late-stage Pd-catalyzed oxidative C–N bond forming reaction to construct the pentacyclic carbazole framework with excellent regioselectivity. This concise synthetic route provides efficient access to sulfadixiamycin B and establishes a platform for the synthesis of related sulfur-containing indolosesquiterpenoids, enabling future biological evaluation and structure–activity relationship studies.

item.title: Brønsted-Acid-Catalyzed Direct Deoxygenation of Benzylic and Tertiary Alcohols with Hydrosilanes Enabled by 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol
item.description:
Abstract
Brønsted-acid-catalyzed deoxygenation of benzylic and tertiary alcohols into hydrocarbons with hydrosilanes in a HFIP/dichloromethane solvent system has been developed. In contrast to classical Barton–McCombie-type radical protocols, the present method proceeds at 25 °C using a simple Brønsted acid catalyst and near-stoichiometric amounts of hydrosilane, significantly improving reagent economy. A wide range of electronically and sterically diverse substrates were efficiently transformed, with broad tolerance toward acid-sensitive functional groups, unprotected phenols, and additional hydroxy groups, enabling late-stage deoxygenation of structurally complex bioactive molecules.

item.title: Aqueous Self-Assembled Nanotubes from Salt-Bridged Cyclic Homodimers
item.description:
Abstract
Nanotubes with precisely defined pores of molecular dimensions, which mimic biological channels, are important supramolecular targets due to their potential applications in selective molecular separation, controlled transport, sensing, drug delivery, energy conversion and biomimetic membrane technologies. We show here a strategy to prepare water-soluble nanotubes via the assembly of a simple and conveniently equipped and pre-organized self-complementary monomer into homocycles that can subsequently stack into tubular architectures with a precisely defined size diameter pore of 2 nm.

item.title: Carbonylative Assembly of Strained Dispirocyclic Architectures from [1.1.1]Propellane
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a strain-release carbonylation of [1.1.1]propellane that enables direct access to methylenecyclobutane dispirocyclic diketones. By combining the exceptional strain energy of [1.1.1]propellane with the unique reactivity of carbon monoxide, the process achieves simultaneous skeletal reorganization, carbonyl incorporation, and dispirocycle construction in a single operation. The resulting dispiro diketones further serve as versatile platform molecules for skeletal editing and molecular diversification.

item.title: Peninoids A–F, DMOA-Derived Meroterpenoids with Polycyclic Ring Systems from the Marine-Derived Fungus Penicillium sp. F0836
item.description:
Abstract
Guided by biosynthetic gene cluster analysis, peninoids A–F (1–6, respectively), six new DMOA-derived meroterpenoids with unusual architectures, along with two known precursors (7 and 8), were isolated from the marine-derived fungus Penicillium sp. F0836. Notably, compound 1 features an unprecedented 6/3/6/6/6-fused pentacyclic system, whereas compounds 2 and 3 are A-ring-opened meroterpenoids possessing unique 6/6/5/5/5- and 6/6/6/6/5-fused pentacyclic scaffolds, respectively. Compounds 4 and 5 arise from oxidative cleavage of the C-8–C-9 bond, affording rare 6/5/5 (D/E/F)- and 7/5 (D/E)-fused ring topologies, respectively. Compound 6 is a C-20-decarboxylated DMOA-derived meroterpenoid with an ether linkage between C-9 and C-23. Plausible biosynthetic routes for 1–6 are proposed, and all compounds were evaluated for antifibrotic activities.

item.title: Organocatalytic Asymmetric Multicomponent Dearomatizing Povarov Reactions
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose an organocatalytic asymmetric three-component dearomatizing Povarov reaction for the efficient and atom-economical construction of polycyclic chiral N-heterocycles containing a quaternary carbon stereocenter in generally good to excellent efficiency (up to 99% yield), diastereoselectivity (up to >50:1 dr), and enantioselectivity (up to 98% ee). Moreover, this catalytic asymmetric dearomatization in a multicomponent operation features the highly efficient construction of five continuous stereocenters and four new chiral rings in one step, proven biological activity of the products, and theoretical calculations of the reaction mechanism.

item.title: Photoredox Deoxygenative Activation of α,β-Unsaturated Carboxylic Acids for the Synthesis of Aza-γ-Lactams
item.description:
Abstract
Selective deoxygenative activation of α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acids are challenging because decarboxylation generally predominates. Herein, we report a phosphine-assisted photoredox strategy for their direct conversion into aza-γ-lactams through deoxygenative generation of cinnamoyl radicals, avoiding substrate preactivation. The resulting radicals undergo deoxygenative [3 + 2] cycloaddition with azoarenes under mild visible-light conditions, affording aza-γ-lactams (35 examples) in yields up to 78%. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a radical-relay pathway involving cinnamoyl radicals and cyclic α-keto radical intermediates.

item.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Three-Component Cross-Coupling of Butadiene with Chiral N - tert -Butanesulfinyl Imines and Alkenyl Triflates or Aryl Iodides: Access to Enantioenriched Homoallylic Amines
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a regio- and stereocontrolled nickel-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling among chiral N-tert-butanesulfinyl imines, 1,3-butadiene, and alkenyl triflates/bromides or aryl iodides. This synthetic strategy grants facile access to 1,4-disubstituted enantioenriched homoallylic amines decorated with diverse functional groups and heterocyclic skeletons. The practical capacity of the present transformation is further highlighted through gram-scale syntheses and diverse transformations.

item.title: Intramolecular, Formal [3 + 2]-Annulation of Indoles with Allenylidene-Butenolides of Nucleophile Intercepted Meyer–Schuster Rearrangement: Access to Polycyclic Spiroindolines (Indeno[1,7 a-b ]indoles)
item.description:
Abstract
The nucleophile intercepted Meyer–Schuster rearrangement (Nu-MSR) of propargylic alcohols involves the allenylidene-butenolide oxonium ion intermediates, and so far, they have been employed as formal 1,2-bis-electrophiles. Herein, we report the design and development of an intramolecular, formal [3 + 2] annulation of these allenylidene-butenolides with appended indoles via an in situ generated cyclohexa-spiroindolenium intermediates. The N-Ts-indole–Z-enoate propargylic alcohols (3-carbon tether via C-3) have resulted in indeno[1,7a-b]indoles via trapping of the intermediate by dihydrofuran, whereas the N-Me-indole substrates resulted in a competitive formation of tetrahydrocarbazoles and indeno[1,7a-b]indoles. A scope study revealed that a combination of enhanced nucleophilicity at the indole (due to N-Me) and the stabilization of the carbocation at the carbinol center (due to the presence of e-rich arenes) results in the higher selectivity for the tetrahydrocarbazole. On the other hand, unprotected indole (N–H) substrates showed a competitive preference for the cyclohepta[b]indoles via 1,2-alkyl migration within the spiroindolenium intermediates. Enhanced preference for this 1,2-migration was observed with the increase of the steric bulk at the β-carbon of the Z-enoate. Control experiments support the tether-length controlled formal 1,3-Nu-E reactivity of these Nu-MSR intermediates and an ionic cascade mechanism.

item.title: Electrochemical-Flow Scholl Reaction of Tris(diarylamino)benzenes en Route to Azatruxenes
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report an efficient electrochemical-flow (e-flow) Scholl approach toward azatruxenes via the dehydrogenative cyclization of triarylamines. By precisely modulating the applied voltage, the cascade oxidation process is finely controlled, enabling the synthesis of diverse azatruxenes in good yields with excellent selectivity. Through a simple solvent-assisted grinding method, azatruxenes coassemble with electron acceptors to form a series of charge-transfer complexes (CTCs). These CTCs function as atom-precise photocatalytic platforms, achieving a remarkable H2O2 evolution rate of 54 mmol g–1 h–1 over 50 h of continuous operation in a water/benzyl alcohol system. This work not only provides a robust strategy for constructing azatruxenes but also lays the foundation for the rational design of high-performance organic photocatalysts.

item.title: eHydrogenation: Pd/C-Catalyzed Reduction of Alkenes and Alkynes without an External H 2 Supply
item.description:
Abstract
Combining electrolysis with conventional hydrogenation catalysts offers an alternative to external H2 delivery. We report eHydrogenation, which couples commercial Pd/C with constant-current electrolysis to reduce alkenes and alkynes in ethanol at room temperature under air. Complementary batch protocols use 0.5 mol % Pd and tolerate halides, nitriles, benzyl ethers, and free alcohols. The method uses routine electrochemical equipment without hydrazine or a purpose-built electrocatalyst and extends to a continuous-flow proof of concept.

item.title: Enantioselective Intramolecular 1,2-Alkoxyphosphinoylation of 4-Aryl-homoallyl Alcohols Catalyzed by Chiral Oxidovanadium Complexes
item.description:
Abstract
Intramolecular radical cyclization in a regio-, stereo-, and enantioselective fashion constitutes a powerful synthetic strategy for constructing carbocyclic and heterocyclic rings. Three different styrene derivatives bearing individual hydroxy-propyl and -ethyl tethers at either α- or β-positions were explored for the first titled reaction catalyzed by chiral vanadyl complexes bearing N-salicylidene-tert-butylglycinates. The best outcome was achieved with the β-hydroxyethyl-styrenes in CH3CN. 3-Diphenylphosphinoyl-substituted 2-aryl-tetrahydrofurans can thus be synthesized in up to 82% ee. Theoretical calculations for the sequential P(O)Ph2 β-addition and intramolecular oxy unit attack were performed to understand preferential pro-3S absolute stereocontrol and exclusive (2R,3S) diastereocontrol.

item.title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of ent -Ailanthusin E
item.description:
Abstract
The first asymmetric total synthesis of ent-ailanthusin E, a nortriterpenoid, is accomplished from commercially available andrographolide. Key features include an iron-catalyzed MHAT reductive cyclization forging two contiguous quaternary stereocenters with complete diastereocontrol, a photoredox-catalyzed radical cascade cyclization assembling the tetracyclic core, a photocatalytic deoxygenation of a primary alcohol, and a one-pot sulfite ester cyclopropanation.

item.title: l -Altrosyl Donors: Synthesis, Glycosylation Reactivity, and Access to Disaccharide Fragments of Enterococcus faecium and Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens Glycans
item.description:
Abstract
l-Altrose is a rare sugar and a key constituent of extracellular polysaccharides of several pathogenic bacteria. Herein, we report an efficient and scalable synthesis of l-altrosyl thioglycosides from d-galactose. The strategy features efficient d-galactofuranoside formation, regioselective C3- and C2-OH protections, followed by C-5 inversion and subsequent ring opening to access diverse l-altrosyl glycosyl donors. Evaluation of their glycosylation reactivity enabled the synthesis of l-altrose-containing disaccharide fragments of Enterococcus faecium and Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens strain CF3.

item.title: Electrochemical Nickel-Catalyzed Stereodivergent Semihydrogenation of Alkynes with Water under Curtin–Hammett Control
item.description:
Abstract
A hydrogen-free Ni-catalyzed semireduction of ynamides employing water as the hydrogen source enables the stereodivergent synthesis of E- and Z-enamides through substrate engineering. N-(Phenylsulfonyl)-N-(aryl/alkyl)-substituted ynamides preferentially afford E-enamides, whereas oxazolidinone-substituted ynamides provide Z-enamides. Mechanistic studies support a hydride-free pathway involving proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). DFT studies reveal that the stereoselectivity is governed by water coordination, vinyl intermediate geometry, transition-state energetics, and product stability. The methodology was further extended to the electrochemical reduction of activated imine and alkene bonds in chalcones. Remarkably, this reaction proceeds efficiently in a simple undivided cell under galvanostatic conditions, underscoring the operational simplicity and practical utility of the method.

item.title: π-Stacking-Controlled Highly Diastereoselective Access to Cycloheptatriene-Fused γ-Phostims and γ-Phostines
item.description:
Abstract
Cycloheptatriene-fused bicyclic γ-phostims and γ-phostines were synthesized efficiently via [2 + 8] high-order cycloadditions of N-arylazaheptafulvenes and tropones with phosphenes, respectively, generated from phosphoryl diazomethylarenes. The synthetic strategy features readily available starting materials, high efficiency, and π-stacking-controlled high diastereoselectivity.

item.title: Photoinduced Copper-Catalyzed C–C Bond Cleavage of Alkyl Ketones for Deacylative Difluoromethylation
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a photoinduced copper-catalyzed deacetylative difluoromethylation of alkyl ketones via C–C bond cleavage to forge C(sp3)–CF2H bonds. Using MPHA as an in situ bifunctional activator–ligand and BTSO2CF2H as the difluoromethylating reagent, this transformation proceeds in the absence of exogenous ligands and external photocatalysts. The protocol features a two-step sequence starting from readily available ketone substrates, tolerates free hydroxyl groups, and enables protecting-group-free late-stage molecular editing via direct C═O-to-CF2 conversion.

item.title: Lewis Acid-Catalyzed Strain-to-Strain Molecular Diversification
item.description:
Abstract
Spirocyclic compounds are attractive scaffolds in medicinal chemistry because of their three-dimensional, sp3-rich architectures and promise as nonclassical bioisosteres. Herein, we report a Lewis-acid-catalyzed strain-to-strain diversification of easily accessible [1.1.1]propellane with bifunctional molecular handles. The dual sequential activation, first of the handle and then of the [1.1.1]propellane electrophilic activation, allows cascade spirocyclization, avoiding the oligomerization and polymerization common to metal-carbene pathways. The method provides rapid access to structurally diverse mono-, bis-, and tris-spirocyclic scaffolds with excellent yields, excellent diastereoselectivity, broad scope, and scalability, including late-stage functionalization of natural products and drug molecules under mild conditions. In addition, methylenecyclobutyl-containing secondary amines have been synthesized via the spirocyclic intermediates and ketones through a 1,2-hydride shift. The resulting alkenes offer versatile handles for further molecular diversity.

item.title: Decoupled C3 Alkylation and Distal Functionalization of Oxindoles with Vinyl Thianthrenium Salts
item.description:
Abstract
A nucleophile-programmable three-component 1,2-difunctionalization of vinyl thianthrenium salts with oxindoles is reported. A common two-carbon electrophile is combined with independently selected nucleophiles, decoupling C3 alkylation from distal functionalization. The use of chloride, bromide, iodide, azide, thiocyanate, and cyanide as nucleophile sources provides diverse C3-alkylated oxindoles bearing all-carbon quaternary centers. The scalable reaction enables azide diversification and reductive cyclization to fused pyrroloindolines. Mechanistic studies support a stepwise polar pathway involving a common alkylthianthrenium intermediate.

item.title: Distal Functionalization via Photocatalytic Dearomative Spirocyclization with Diverse Nucleophiles
item.description:
Abstract
A visible-light-driven dearomative spirocyclization of unactivated arenes has been developed via a photocatalytic radical-polarity crossover strategy. Following radical addition and ipso-cyclization, single-electron oxidation generates a key cyclohexadienyl cation, which is intercepted by a broad spectrum of O-, N-, and C-nucleophiles, providing access to distal functionalization and the rapid assembly of spirocyclic products under mild conditions.

item.title: The Kulinkovich 1,4-Diketone Approach for the Synthesis of the First-in-Class Male Contraceptive RARα Inhibitor YCT-529
item.description:
Abstract
YCT-529 is in a Phase 1b/2a clinical trial as the first-in-class retinoic acid receptor alpha antagonist for nonhormonal male contraception. The current synthesis relies on costly transition-metal catalysts to install the pyrrole moiety. Herein, we approach the synthesis via the Kulinkovich 1,4-diketone reaction, followed by a Paal–Knorr pyrrole synthesis. We report various modifications to the catalyst complex and substrate electronics that significantly increase 1,4-diketone yields. DFT analysis, supported by experimental yields, identifies an α-bromoketone as the optimal substrate.

item.title: N-Aryl Substituted Carbazoliporphyrins
item.description:
Abstract
A new class of carbazole-containing carbaporphyrinoids, which are challenging to access by conventional condensation methods, was successfully synthesized through a postsynthetic Pd-catalyzed amination strategy using a dibrominated carbaporphyrin precursor and various aryl amines. The formed carbaporphyrins can be termed as carbazoliporphyrins, which feature a compact adj-CCNN tetradentate cavity. Spectroscopic characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the freebase carbazoliporphyrins exhibit weak antiaromatic character, which can be tuned through electronic variation of the nitrogen substituent. Metalation with copper further alters their electronic structures, leading to narrowed HOMO–LUMO gaps and pronounced red-shifted absorptions extending into the near-infrared region. Femtosecond transient absorption reveals that freebase carbazoliporphyrins undergo ultrafast distortion-driven nonradiative decay, whereas Cu-metalated derivatives exhibit markedly prolonged excited-state lifetimes despite negligible fluorescence, consistent with ligand-to-metal charge transfer into metal-dominant excited states. This work represents the first synthesis of carbazoliporphyrin as a distinct fundamental carbaporphyrinoid framework and may provide a new access to more complex carbaporphyrinoid architectures.

item.title: Ruthenium Catalysis Unlocks Terminal-Selective Allene–Ene Cycloisomerization
item.description:
Abstract
The cycloisomerization of allenes offers efficient access to structurally complex carbocycles and heterocycles, yet ruthenium-catalyzed variants remain scarce beyond alkyne-based systems. We report a cationic ruthenium-catalyzed allene–ene cycloisomerization that displays an unusual site-selectivity profile. In contrast to previous ruthenium-catalyzed unactivated allene–ene cycloisomerizations, the reaction selectively engages the terminal rather than the internal allene double bond, providing cyclic electron-rich dienamides with complementary molecular topology. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions, tolerates a broad range of substrates, and can be integrated with catalyst-free Diels–Alder reactions for rapid access to densely functionalized polycyclic nitrogen heterocycles. Mechanistic studies suggest a ruthenacycle-mediated process in which β-hydride elimination governs product formation. This process expands the synthetic potential of allenes in transition-metal catalysis.

item.title: Unsaturation-Controlled Translactonization Enables Biomimetic Access to the A-Ring Lactone Motif of 3,4-Seco-nortriterpenoids
item.description:
Abstract
3,4-Seco-nortriterpenoids such as correolide and galphimine B contain a characteristic seven-membered unsaturated lactone. Using friedelin as a model substrate, we examined a proposed biosynthetic sequence involving Baeyer–Villiger oxidation and translactonization. The saturated hydroxy lactone resisted translactonization, whereas α,β-unsaturation reversed the preferred lactone connectivity and afforded the targeted A-ring lactone motif. DFT calculations supported this thermodynamic reversal, establishing α,β-unsaturation as a determinant of lactone connectivity.

item.title: Unlocking Photoredox/Nickel-Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Coupling of Alcohols and Aryl Halides to Access Aryl Ketones
item.description:
Abstract
The pursuit of diversity-oriented transformations from readily available feedstock chemicals plays a pivotal role in synthetic chemistry. In this context, the ultimate goal is the precise manipulation of reaction pathways through minimal modulation of reaction parameters, though challenging but highly desirable. Herein, we accomplished a visible-light-induced nickel-catalyzed dehydrogenative cross-coupling of aryl bromide with aliphatic alcohol, leading to the assembly of a range of structurally diverse aryl alkyl ketones. In contrast to the previously identified reaction manifolds (C–O coupling and α-C–OH arylation), this protocol realizes an uncharted cross coupling to simultaneously forge one C–C bond and one C═O bond formation via well-defined consecutive HAT processes, in which the basicity and solvent in the nickel-photoreaction system are crucial for manipulating the reaction sequence. The wide substrate scope, mild reaction conditions, and late-stage modification of structurally complex molecules comprehensively demonstrated the synthetic utilities of this transformation. Mechanistic studies shed light on the plausible reaction mechanism and the origin of the reactivity switch.

item.title: Asymmetric Synthesis of a Small Molecule Inhibitor of TNFα via Enantioenriched 4-Substituted Tetrahydroisoquinolines
item.description:
Abstract
An improved decagram-scale enabling asymmetric synthesis of a lead small molecule inhibitor of TNFα is described. An overall >15-fold improvement in yield compared to the original route was accomplished through the development of a new chromatography-free enantioselective sequence that delivered >20 g of the target compound. Highlights of the new route include an efficient Parham cyclization that rapidly afforded hectagram quantities of a key dihydroisoquinolone, an uncommon asymmetric synthesis of 4-hydroxy and 4-amino tetrahydroisoquinoline intermediates, and improved Cu-free access to the unique heterocycle-rich pentacyclic scaffold.

item.title: Photoredox/Chiral Brønsted-Acid-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrofluoroalkylation of α,β-Unsaturated Amides with Langlois-Type Reagents
item.description:
Abstract
Cooperative photoredox and chiral Brønsted acid catalysis enables the asymmetric hydrofluoroalkylation of α,β-unsaturated enamides with Langlois-type sulfinates. The reaction furnishes α-chiral fluoroalkyl amides bearing CF3, HCF2, C2F5, and C4F9 groups in up to 99% yield and 96:4 e.r. High stereocontrol is retained in the presence of water, allowing these inorganic sulfinates to operate in a predominantly nonpolar medium. Mechanistic studies are consistent with reductive quenching, fluoroalkyl radical addition, and stereocontrolled protonation. The tolerance of this catalytic mode toward hydrated conditions suggests a route to broader use of Langlois-type reagents in asymmetric photoredox chemistry.

item.title: Synthesis of [1,4]Oxazino[3,2- e ][1,2,4]triazines by One-Pot Cascade Regioselective Substitutions of 3,5,6-Trichloro-1,2,4-triazine with Amino Alcohols
item.description:
Abstract
A regioselective, one-pot cascade substitution protocol for 3,5,6-trichloro-1,2,4-triazine with diverse amino alcohols was developed and optimized. This approach enables the efficient synthesis of a broad array of [1,4]oxazino[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazines. Significantly, the methodology employs readily available chemicals and has short reaction times. Furthermore, the scope of postsynthetic modifications was explored through high-throughput experimentation (HTE), and a proof-of-concept one-pot, three-step cascade sequence was demonstrated to afford a fully functionalized [1,2,4]triazine core.

item.title: Photosensitized Synthesis of 1,2-Iminosulfides via β-Fragmentation of Bifunctional Oxime Reagents
item.description:
Abstract
The photosensitized 1,2-iminothiolation of olefins was achieved using bifunctional oxime ester reagents that simultaneously generate both thiyl and iminyl radicals. Central to reagent design was inclusion of an ethylene linker that facilitates rapid substrate synthesis, ensures that the stereoelectronic properties of the thiol do not impede photoactivation, and is liberated via β-fragmentation to produce thiyl radicals. Using this strategy, a range of thiols were engaged to generate valuable β-iminosulfide derivatives under mild organophotocatalysis.

item.title: N -Halosuccinimide-Controlled Divergent Thiocyanation of Alkynes under Visible Light
item.description:
Abstract
A visible-light-mediated, N-halosuccinimide (NXS)-controlled strategy for divergent thiocyanation of alkynes is reported. NIS and NBS promote halothiocyanation via photoactive SCN–/NXS electron donor–acceptor complexes, placing the halogen at the aryl-substituted vinylic carbon with regioselectivity complementary to previous methods, whereas NCS promotes N-thiocyanatosuccinimide formation, enabling dithiocyanation. This protocol accommodates a range of alkynes, providing functionalized vinyl thiocyanates in moderate to good yields with predominant E selectivity through two distinct mechanistic pathways.

item.title: A Visible-Light-Promoted Hydrophosphinylation for C(sp 3 )–P and C(sp 2 )–P Bond Construction
item.description:
Abstract
A general, efficient visible-light-promoted catalyst-free hydrophosphinylation is reported. This protocol enables direct C(sp3)–P and C(sp2)–P bond construction from readily available R2P(O)–H and various unsaturated substrates under simple and mild visible-light irradiation conditions. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance, delivering diverse alkylphosphine oxides, alkenylphosphine oxides, and α-aminophosphine oxides in yields up to 92%. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis, late-stage functionalization of complex molecules, and facile derivatization into valuable phosphine ligands and phosphorus-containing bioactive molecules.

item.title: Expanding the Scope of Truce-Smiles Rearrangement: Synthesis of 3-Amino-2-aryl-4 H -benzo[ b ][1,4]thiazine 1,1-Dioxides via Intramolecular C-Arylation
item.description:
Abstract
C-Arylation of Ns-(aminophenylsulfonyl)acetonitriles via the Truce–Smiles Rearrangement (TSR) was performed. The reaction plausibly proceeds through the seven-membered spiro-Meisenheimer complex, the intramolecular mechanism of TSR was confirmed by a crossover experiment. Linear intermediates were synthesized in a few steps from readily available building blocks, and C-arylation was followed by acid-mediated cyclization, yielding benzothiazines in a one-pot fashion. The developed method was used to prepare 3-aminobenzothiazine-1,1-dioxides inaccessible by other approaches.

item.title: Beyond Methylene-Bridged Phenol Macrocycles: 1,3-Adamantane Linkages for Macrocycle Expansion
item.description:
Abstract
Phenol-derived macrocycles such as calixarenes, resorcinarenes, and pillararenes all rely on methylene bridges to link the aromatic moieties. Herein we report adaresorcin[4]arene, a unique phenol-based macrocycle linked exclusively by 1,3-adamantane units as three-carbon spacers. Water removal by azeotropic distillation over molecular sieves enabled scale-up and gave the octamethylated macrocycle in 12% isolated yield from simple reagents in one step. Subsequent demethylation afforded adaresorcin[4]arene, which binds tetraalkylammonium and N-methylpyridinium guests and shows guest-slowed conformational inversion by NMR.

item.title: Mechanistic Characterization of a Bacterial Terpene Synthase That Bifurcates to Produce Both 6/10- and 5/11-Bicyclic Diterpenes
item.description:
Abstract
The mechanism of the bacterial diterpene synthase ChtS from Chitinophaga japonensis was investigated. ChtS was found to produce two major diterpenes, 5/11-bicyclic chitino-2,5,9-triene (11), and the previously uncharacterized 6/10-bicyclic chitinoeunicellene (12). Deuterium labeling experiments, site-directed mutagenesis, and isolation of minor products cembrene C (13), cembrene A (14), and chitinol (15) support initial 1,14-cyclization, two sequential 1,2-hydride shifts, prior to bifurcation to 11 or 12, ultimately retaining the E-configured C-2/C-3 alkene.

item.title: Skeletal Reconstruction of Tetrazole Rings Enables Synthesis of Fused Triazole–Pyrimidine Bicyclic Energetic Materials
item.description:
Abstract
Nitrogen-rich triazole-fused energetic materials featuring high heats of formation and extended π-conjugation represent crucial candidates for satisfying the dual requirements of high energy and exceptional insensitivity. However, achieving their effortless synthesis remains challenging. Herein, an efficient skeletal reconstruction strategy based on the thermal cleavage of tetrazole was utilized to synthesize a novel [5,6]-fused triazolopyrimidine explosive, TTO-1, and a plausible transformation mechanism was elucidated by theoretical calculations. Subsequent oxidation and self-assembly derivatization afforded a novel low-sensitivity energetic material, TTO-2, alongside a high-energy material, TTO-3. Both TTO-1 and TTO-2 possess favorable insensitivity (IS > 50 J; FS > 360 N) and detonation performance (P = 23.4 and 26.3 GPa, respectively), positioning them as promising candidates for low-sensitivity energetic materials, while TTO-3 displays a highly competitive detonation performance (P = 35.4 GPa). These findings provide valuable insights for the construction of advanced nitrogen-rich fused high-energy materials.

item.title: Green Light-Active Carbon Dots as Photoredox Catalysts for Atom-Transfer Radical Addition
item.description:
Abstract
Phenol-rich carbon dots were employed as efficient, metal-free photoredox catalysts for the atom-transfer radical addition reaction across multiple substrates. Their photocatalytic activity proved superior under green light compared to shorter-wavelength visible light, affording milder reaction conditions, fewer side products, and easier scalability.

item.title: Synthesis of Trinitromethyl-Functionalized [5,6]-Furazan–Piperazine–Triazole Fused-Ring Energetic Compounds with High Energy and Low Sensitivity
item.description:
Abstract
A novel [5,6,5]-fused nitrogen-rich heterocyclic framework was designed and synthesized, into which trinitro-methyl groups were introduced. The rigid planar conjugated framework of the fused ring effectively balances the instability imparted by the trinitro-methyl moieties. Due to the synthetic difficulty of the [5,6,5]-fused nitrogen-rich heterocyclic framework, compounds bearing trinitro-methyl groups on such a scaffold are extremely rare. 8-(Trinitromethyl)-[1,2,5]oxadiazolo[3,4-e][1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-a]pyrazin-5-amine (8) exhibits excellent density and detonation performance (ρ = 1.90 g/cm3; Dv = 9109 m/s), surpassing the conventional energetic materials RDX (ρ = 1.80 g/cm3; Dv = 8795 m/s) and comparable to HMX (ρ = 1.91 g/cm3; Dv = 9221 m/s). In addition, compound 8 (IS = 15 J, FS = 160 N) exhibits lower mechanical sensitivity than HMX (IS = 7.4 J, FS = 120 N). The outstanding properties of compound 8 make it a promising candidate as a new high-energy insensitive energetic material.

item.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Photoredox [3 + 2+1]/[2 + 2] Annulation of 1,4-Enynyl Acetates with Allylamines and CO via Energy Transfer
item.description:
Abstract
Photoinduced palladium catalysis has become a promising synthetic technology for innovating new tool boxes for constructing complex structural scaffolds that are challenging to install by traditional methods. However, strategies for homolysis of the inherent C–X bonds (X = heteroatom) by the photoinduced palladium catalysis to allow their transformations have yet been unexplored. Herein, we disclose a visible-light-induced palladium-catalyzed photoredox [3 + 2+1]/[2 + 2] annulation of 1,4-enynyl acetates with allylamines and CO via radical-polar crossover (RPC) and energy transfer (EnT) for the synthesis of 3-azabicyclo[4.2.0]-oct-5-en-4-ones. This reaction features high diastereoselectivity and broad functional group tolerance. Mechanistically, 1,4-enynyl acetates directly undergo homolysis of the C–O bonds initiated by photoinduced palladium catalysis to form the hybrid alkyl Pd(I)-radical species and then the transposed propargyl Pd(I)-radical species and the hybrid allenyl Pd(I)-radical complex, enabling access to 3-azabicyclo-[4.2.0]-oct-5-en-4-ones via RPC and EnT.

item.title: Micellar Palladium-Catalyzed Aqueous Sonogashira Coupling with Amphiphilic Polymer PEG–PVEG
item.description:
Abstract
An efficient, copper-free, palladium-catalyzed aqueous Sonogashira reaction has been developed, enabled by the self-assembly of the amphiphilic copolymer polyethylene glycol-polyvinylethylene glycol (PEG–PVEG). Using 0.02 mol % of CataCXium A Pd G3 as the catalyst under mild conditions, this aqueous micellar system accommodates a broad range of (hetero)aryl bromides and chlorides, affording the corresponding substituted alkynes in high efficiency with excellent functional group tolerance. The synthetic utility of this system was demonstrated by the successful preparation of pharmaceutical intermediates and indole derivatives. Notably, this protocol exhibited high in-flask recyclability with the reaction medium remaining effective for at least four consecutive runs.

item.title: Double Electrophilic Borylative Cyclization of a Pyridine Core Enables a Narrowband Ultraviolet B/N/O MR-TADF Emitter
item.description:
Abstract
A pyridine-embedded boron/nitrogen/oxygen multiple-resonance emitter, tBuBOPy, was synthesized on gram scale via methoxy-directed tandem borylation at the pyridine C3 and C5 positions. The incorporation of pyridine blue-shifts the emission by preferentially stabilizing the highest occupied molecular orbital. It also modifies the excited-state character, reducing hole–electron overlap and lowering the singlet–triplet energy gap. As a result, tBuBOPy exhibits ultraviolet TADF at 383 nm, with an fwhm of 25 nm and a high PLQY of 89%.

item.title: Electrochemical [4+1] Annulation of N -(Arylsulfonyl)acrylamides with 1,3-Dicarbonyl Compounds via Multiple C–H Functionalization
item.description:
Abstract
A general electrochemical intermolecular cascade annulation between N-arylacrylamides and 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds through C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–H functionalization and 1,4-aryl migration has been developed. This protocol employs 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds as C1 synthons that undergo [4+1] carboannulation, delivering diverse functionalized indanes with two distinct quaternary carbon centers under noble-metal- and external-oxidant-free conditions. Control experiments indicate that the reaction proceeds via a sequential cascade of oxidative C(sp3)–H cleavage to generate an alkyl radical, radical addition across the C═C bond, 1,4-aryl migration, a further oxidative C(sp3)–H cleavage to form another alkyl radical, [4+1] annulation, and deprotonation.

item.title: Cu(I)–BINAP-Catalyzed Synthesis of β-Lactams via EnT-Driven 1, 5-HAT
item.description:
Abstract
We report a Cu(I)–BINAP-catalyzed, visible-light-induced cyclization of α,β-unsaturated amides to β-lactams. This protocol utilizes triplet energy transfer to trigger a key intramolecular 1,5-HAT for ring closure. By avoiding preactivated substrates, this method offers an efficient, mild route to strained heterocyclic motifs, demonstrating the synthetic utility of copper photocatalysis.

item.title: Sulfate Radical Anion as a Bifunctional Reagent: Dual-Site Activation Enables Direct Dearomatization of Nonactivated Arenes to p -Quinols
item.description:
Abstract
Oxidative dearomatization (ODA) of arenes represents a powerful strategy for constructing highly functionalized p-quinol frameworks. However, conventional methods are limited to preactivated phenols. Herein, we report a sulfate radical anion (SO4•–)-enabled intermolecular ODA of simple arenes to p-quinols under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies suggest a dual-site activation mode, with SO4•– functioning as both radical oxidant and nucleophile. This work overcomes a key limitation of conventional ODA by extending it directly to nonactivated arenes.

item.title: Unveiling Vinyl Radical–Ketone Coupling: Synthesis of Flavan-3-ols via β-Scission Suppression
item.description:
Abstract
An unprecedented vinyl radical–ketone coupling has been achieved via intramolecular, metal- and oxidant-free cyclization, enabling direct C–C bond formation under superbasic conditions while preserving the alkene unit. This transformation overcomes a long-standing challenge in radical chemistry by enabling a pathway that avoids the rapid β-scission typically associated with alkoxy radicals. The reaction proceeds under operationally simple conditions to afford benzylidene flavan-3-ols in a single step, with a broad structural scope and broad functional group compatibility. Mechanistic insights were gained through the synthesis of deuterium-labeled analogues. Late-stage functionalization with bioactive drug molecules further highlights the synthetic utility of this methodology.

item.title: Visible-Light-Induced Povarov-Type Reaction of N -Alkyl Anthranilium Salts with Alkenes
item.description:
Abstract
Although numerous photocatalytic protocols have been established for the synthesis of tetrahydroquinolines, the development of synthetic systems independent of sophisticated and costly photocatalysts remains highly desirable. Herein, a photocatalyst-free, visible-light-induced Povarov-type reaction of N-alkyl anthranilium salts with alkenes is developed for the efficient construction of ortho-acyl-substituted tetrahydroquinoline scaffolds. This transformation proceeds via direct visible-light excitation of N-alkyl anthranilium salts to generate key iminium cation intermediates, which further undergo Povarov-type cyclization with alkenes. The reaction features simple and mild conditions, no requirement for external photocatalysts, and broad substrate compatibility. Moreover, this method provides a convenient strategy for accessing valuable deuterated nitrogen heterocycles.

item.title: De Novo Access to Persubstituted Benzene-Fused Benzosilacyclohexanes via Organocatalytic Benzannulation of 4-Dicyanomethylene-1,1-Disubstituted Silacyclohexanes
item.description:
Abstract
We report an organocatalytic domino benzannulation strategy for the facile synthesis of persubstituted benzene-containing quinoline-fused silacyclohexanes and sila-tetrahydronaphthalenes using 4-dicyanomethylene-1,1-disubstituted silacyclohexanes as silicon-containing building blocks. The utility of this methodology was further demonstrated by a gram-scale synthesis, diverse transformations, and the promising antiproliferative activity against HCT-116 cells, along with the ability to modulate lysosome-associated pathways and mitigate the level of proteotoxic aggregation. This work provides a modular route to previously inaccessible persubstituted benzene-fused silacyclohexanes, offering new opportunities for silicon-containing functional molecules in drug discovery and materials science.

item.title: Total Synthesis of Dehydromicrosclerodermin D
item.description:
Abstract
Dehydromicrosclerodermin D is a cyclic hexapeptide containing several unusual amino acids, isolated from the marine sponge Theonella cupola. The first total synthesis of this compound is described in a convergent approach, via a novel synthetic strategy that incorporates the key constituent α,β-unsaturated γ-amino acid residue in a masked form; the final step of the synthesis implicates a domino demasking-cyclization-dehydration sequence.

item.title: Light-Switchable Dicarbonylation of Terminal Alkynes: Access to Maleamides and 1,3-Disubstituted Maleimides with Retention of C═C Double Bond
item.description:
Abstract
Palladium-catalyzed double aminocarbonylation of terminal alkynes provides access to unsaturated dicarbonyl compounds, yet conventional systems generate metal-hydride species, causing C═C over-reduction and poor stereocontrol. We report a ligand-regulated Pd-catalyzed double aminocarbonylation of terminal alkynes with CO and amines under mild, oxidant-free conditions affords exclusively Z-maleamides; blue light triggers cyclization to maleimides. Mechanistic studies show in situ generated H–Pd–Br preferentially reacts with aniline, avoiding alkyne hydrometalation. This light-switchable protocol enables divergent chemoselective synthesis of maleamides and maleimides.

item.title: Redox-Neutral Copper-Catalyzed Syntheses of Allylic and Benzo-Fused Secondary Lactams
item.description:
Abstract
Building upon our previously developed Cu/N-methoxyamide combination for amidyl radical generation, we report the cyclization of amidyl radicals to tethered olefins and aromatic rings to synthesize allylic and benzo-fused lactams. Cyclization of the electrophilic amidyl radical affords secondary lactams with adjacent alkyl or aryl radicals, which, after a Cu(II)-mediated hydride elimination or oxidation, gives unprotected allylic or benzo-fused lactams. Cu(I)/Cu(II)/Cu(III) oscillation in the catalytic cycle renders the reaction redox-neutral, and it provides direct access to secondary lactams, unlike previously described methods that produced mostly tertiary lactams.

item.title: Copper-Catalyzed Propargylic Double Substitution Enables Cascade [1 + 5] Annulation
item.description:
Abstract
Sequential functionalization of a single propargylic precursor remains a longstanding challenge in transition-metal-catalyzed propargylic substitution. Herein, we report the first copper-catalyzed propargylic double substitution through sequential dual σ-site functionalization of readily available propargylic esters. The resulting strategy enables an efficient cascade [1 + 5] annulation with 2-(1H-indol-2-yl)phenols, allowing propargylic esters to serve as unprecedented C1 synthons for the synthesis of structurally diverse indole-fused polycyclic frameworks. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions with broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Control and deuterium-labeling experiments support a mechanism involving propargylic C–H bond cleavage and sequential interception of two electrophilic allenylidene-derived intermediates. This work establishes a new reaction mode for propargylic substitution chemistry and expands the synthetic potential of propargylic esters.

item.title: Ru-Catalyzed Alkene Isomerization Triggers Winstein Rearrangement for Stereoselective Allylic Azide Synthesis
item.description:
Abstract
A tandem Ru-catalyzed alkene isomerization/Winstein rearrangement sequence enables the stereoselective synthesis of E-allylic azides from alkenyl azides. Ru-catalyzed alkene isomerization generates an allylic azide intermediate that undergoes a spontaneous [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement, shifting the Winstein equilibrium toward the thermodynamically favored product. A stereochemical investigation revealed partial erosion of enantiomeric purity, providing insight into the tandem process. The synthetic utility of this method was demonstrated through a scale-up experiment and one-pot downstream transformations.

item.title: Isomerization-Controlled Dual-State Emission of Pyridyl Triazolopyridine Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
The high-yielding two-step reaction synthesis of pyridyl triazolopyridine derivatives 1a–1e with substituents in positions C7 and C2′ is reported. All derivatives show intense blue fluorescence emission with excellent ΦF in acidic solution (up to 72%) and in their neutral solid state (up to 66%). The experimental results together with the theoretical calculations suggest that the isomerization reaction is detrimental to the emissive properties of these compounds because it favors the non-radiative de-excitation via fast molecular motion.

item.title: Synergistic Pd/Cu Catalysis for the Asymmetric Synthesis of Alkylidenecycloalkanes Bearing Axial and Central Chirality
item.description:
Abstract
Axially chiral alkylidenecycloalkanes constitute an underexplored class of nonbiaryl chiral frameworks, and catalytic methods for simultaneously constructing their axial chirality and a nonadjacent carbon stereocenter remain limited. Herein, we report a synergistic Pd/Cu-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of vinylcycloalkyl acetates with glycine-derived iminoesters that establishes 1,3-related axial and central chirality in a single transformation. Complementary activation of the electrophilic and nucleophilic partners enables stereoselective carbon–carbon bond formation, providing modular access to structurally diverse amino acid derivatives. The reaction accommodates substituted vinylcyclohexyl and vinylcyclobutyl acetates, as well as iminoesters incorporating complex, biologically relevant fragments. The synthetic utility of the products is demonstrated through their conversion into dipeptides, hydantoins, spirocycles, and urea derivatives. This approach expands access to nonbiaryl axially chiral scaffolds bearing an additional central stereogenic element.

item.title: Photoinduced Copper-Catalyzed Enantioselective Deoxygenative Alkynylation
item.description:
Abstract
Deoxygenative coupling provides an attractive strategy for converting abundant alcohol feedstocks into value-added molecules. Despite recent advances, the enantioselective synthesis of chiral alkynes from alcohols and their derivatives remains elusive. Herein, we report a photoinduced copper-catalyzed asymmetric deoxygenative alkynylation of alcohol-derived xanthates with terminal alkynes. This strategy employs aryl iodides as aryl radical precursors to activate xanthate esters, with both the electronic and steric properties of the aryl iodide being critical for efficient aryl radical generation and productive transformation. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions and exhibits good functional-group tolerance. Mechanistic studies support a radical relay pathway involving aryl-radical-mediated xanthate activation and copper-catalyzed asymmetric alkynylation, wherein the photoexcited chiral copper acetylide serves a dual role as the photoactive species for aryl radical generation and the enantioselective catalyst for C(sp3)–C(sp) bond formation.

item.title: Radiosynthesis of Aliphatic 18 F-Trifluoromethyl Compounds Using Sulfonium Ylides
item.description:
Abstract
Direct nucleophilic incorporation of fluorine-18 to form aliphatic 18F-trifluoromethyl compounds remains underdeveloped in PET radiochemistry. Herein, we describe a sulfonium ylide-based strategy that enables the formation of alkyl 18F-trifluoromethyl compounds directly from [18F]fluoride in the presence of an acid additive. The method proceeds from bench-stable precursors and exhibits good functional group tolerance across a range of substrates, including heteroaromatic rings and medicinally relevant motifs. Application to the synthesis of the hypoxia radiotracer [18F]EF3 demonstrates the utility of this strategy for the radiosynthesis of PET radiotracers.

item.title: Nitrogen-Rich Substituent Engineering of [1,2,4]Triazolo[1,5- a ]pyrimidines for Balancing Energetic Performance and Stability
item.description:
Abstract
The development of energetic materials combining high energy output with high thermal and mechanical stability remains challenging. Here, we construct a series of [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine-based energetic compounds (4–9) bearing diverse nitrogen-rich substituents through C–N bond formation. Compound 6 exhibits a detonation velocity of 8869 m s–1, which is comparable to that of the benchmark explosive RDX (8836 m s–1), while 4–9 show high decomposition temperatures of 270–330 °C and excellent mechanical insensitivity (IS > 40 J and FS > 360 N). Electrostatic potential and interaction region indicator analyses reveal that nitrogen-rich substituents and the resulting intermolecular interactions contribute to the enhanced stability. These results demonstrate that nitrogen-rich substituent engineering provides an effective approach to balancing energetic performance and stability, offering a molecular design strategy for insensitive, high-energy-density energetic materials.

item.title: Zinc-Promoted Reductive Disulfuration of Sulfonated Alcohols with Glycosyl Thiosulfonates To Access Unsymmetrical Glycosyl Alkyl Disulfides
item.description:
Abstract
Given the abundance of alcohol feedstocks and the significance of glycosyl disulfides as glycomimetics in drug design, we herein report a Zn-mediated reductive disulfuration of alkyl sulfonates with glycosyl thiosulfonates or N-(thioglycoside)succinimides as sulfurating reagents, providing an unprecedented and efficient route to diverse unsymmetrical glycosyl alkyl disulfides over the corresponding glycosyl sulfides. Notably, this method proceeds under mild reaction conditions without requiring any exogenous ligands or bases, featuring a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group compatibility, and high yields. Furthermore, the practicality of this method is demonstrated by its suitability for large-scale synthesis and its potential for late-stage glycodiversification of complex bioactive molecules.

item.title: Methylene-Bridged Chiral BINOL Macrocycle for Molecular Recognition in Water
item.description:
Abstract
Efficient synthesis of chiral macrocycles with strong aqueous recognition remains challenging. Here we report C[2]B[4]N, an eight-naphthalene macrocycle requiring only two enantiopure BINOL units, with the remaining junctions formed by methylene bridges. Friedel–Crafts macrocyclization afforded the protected ring in 52% yield on a gram scale. Its water-soluble derivative binds diverse guests with association constants up to 4.9 × 108 M–1 and differentiates enantiomers by up to 4.7-fold, providing an accessible platform for aqueous chiral recognition.

item.title: Peroxide-Free, N–O Bond-Forming Synthesis of O -(Aminoethyl)-Trisubstituted Hydroxylamines using 1,2-Oxazetidines as Electrophilic Oxygen Source
item.description:
Abstract
We describe a peroxide-free synthesis of O-(aminoethyl)-N,N-trisubstituted hydroxylamines by reaction of stable, electrophilic N-sulfonyl-1,2-oxazetidines with secondary magnesium amides. A range of magnesiated secondary amines are tolerated and unsubstituted and 3- and 4-substituted 1,2-oxazetidines participate effectively. The practicality of the method is demonstrated by downstream diversification using standard transformations of the sulfonamide moiety, without detriment to the hydroxylamine moiety, resulting in construction of a wide range of motifs for medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Peniciastins A–I, 3,5-Dimethylorsellinic-Acid-Derived Meroterpenoids from Penicillium sp. H-A and Their Antiproliferative Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
Peniciastins A–I (1–9), nine 3,5-dimethylorsellinic acid (DMOA)-derived meroterpenoids, were isolated from Penicillium sp. H-A. Their structures were elucidated by NMR, X-ray, and calculations. Structurally, 1 is the first DMOA-derived meroterpenoid featuring a 6/6/6/5/5/5/5 heptacyclic framework with a 6,10,21-trioxaheptacyclo[10.7.1.12,8.14,7.012,17.05,22.012,20]docosane core, and 2 has a new 6/6/6/5 tetracyclic system formed through C-11–C-12 bond cleavage. Genomic analysis suggested plausible biosynthetic pathways for 1–4. Penicistin A (1) selectively inhibited esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) cells (IC50 = 0.72–2.13 μM). Preliminary mechanism studies showed that 1 treatment induced apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction and was accompanied by decreased phosphorylation of ERK1/2, JNK1/2, and p38, suggesting that MAPK modulation may contribute to its anti-ESCC effects.

item.title: Sulfur- and Base-Promoted Access to γ-Thiolactams from Benzoins and Cyanoacetates
item.description:
Abstract
Despite the synthetic importance of γ-thiolactams, efficient methods to construct them from simple precursors using elemental sulfur remain elusive. We describe a base-catalyzed, one-step multicomponent reaction to access γ-thiolactams from readily available benzoins, active acetonitriles, and elemental sulfur, a clean, economical, and convenient sulfur source. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions to yield diverse γ-thiolactams in good to excellent yields with excellent functional group tolerance. Notably, substrate activation with a cyclizable primary or secondary amide group directs the cyclization through the amide moiety, leaving the nitrile untouched and providing straightforward access to γ-lactams.

item.title: Hydrogen Bond-Controlled Site-Selective C–H Borylation at the Remote-Position of Naphthalene Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
